windshield.strip: 'eyebrow' on the top edge in front of the operator, not extending more than five inches down from the top center of the windshield

frontSide.note: 1994 and later models: at least 25% net light transmission

backSide.note: side windows immediately behind the driver: at least 25% net (passenger cars)

rear.note: rearmost window: at least 10% net light transmission

backSide.note: trucks, buses, trailers, motor homes, multipurpose passenger vehicles: side windows behind the driver at least 10% net

tint.certificateOrSticker: Label on the front glass to the operator's left with the installer's name and phone number affirming all tinting conforms (§ 27-37-306(c))

medicalExemption.text: Physician diagnosis of a disease or disorder (e.g. albinism, lupus) with certification carried in the vehicle; allows at least 20% on front and adjacent side windows, 10% rearmost, 50% windshield; certification valid 3 years

penalty.text: Class B misdemeanor for installers and for operating a vehicle with non-compliant tint

tint.lastAmended: medical-waiver limits effective August 16, 2013 (per statute text); text read as 'current as of March 28, 2024' on FindLaw
quotes: (b)(1) eyebrow: may not extend downward more than "five inches (5")" from the top center of the windshield

(b)(2): side windows "at least twenty-five percent (25%) net light transmission"; trucks, buses, trailers, motor homes, multipurpose passenger vehicles behind driver "at least ten percent (10%) net light transmission"
(b)(3): rearmost window "at least ten percent (10%) net light transmission"
(e)(2): medical: side windows "at least twenty percent (20%) net light transmission"; windshield "at least fifty percent (50%) net light transmission"
(g): "shall be guilty of a Class B misdemeanor"

helmet.conditions: Operators and passengers must wear protective headgear unless 21 or older

handheldPhone.noviceOrAgeBan: Drivers under 18 may not use a wireless telecommunications device or hands-free device except in an emergency (§ 27-51-1603)

radarDetector.note: No Arkansas ban found; commercial vehicles over 10,001 lb banned federally (49 CFR 392.71)
